info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary:
listKeys returns the SSH public keys registered to the caller's org — the keys
that authenticate `git clone git@<host>:<org>/<repo>.git`.
get.description:
listKeys returns the SSH public keys registered to the caller's org — the keys
that authenticate `git clone git@<host>:<org>/<repo>.git`. Keys are org-scoped
on read even though the fingerprint index is global, so one org never sees
another's.

delete.summary:
deleteKey removes a registered SSH key, scoped to the caller's org: an org can
only delete its own, and a key id it does not own is not found.
delete.description:
deleteKey removes a registered SSH key, scoped to the caller's org: an org can
only delete its own, and a key id it does not own is not found. Answers 204
with no body. Once removed the key no longer authenticates any SSH git access.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the key's identifier ("gitkey_…"), from the :id path segment.

get.summary:
listRepos returns the repos in the caller's scope, most recently updated
first.
get.description:
listRepos returns the repos in the caller's scope, most recently updated
first. The scope is the request principal's — the gateway-minted org and its
optional project — never anything off the wire, so a caller only ever sees its
own. Rows carry no branches or HEAD; read one repo for those.

delete.summary: deleteRepo removes a repo's metadata and purges its storage.
delete.description:
deleteRepo removes a repo's metadata and purges its storage. Answers 204 with
no body. The metadata row is the source of truth for existence, so a storage
purge that fails is logged and the delete still succeeds — and a second call
is a 404, not a second delete.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

get.summary:
getRepo returns one repo with its live ref state: every branch name and the
resolved HEAD commit.
get.description:
getRepo returns one repo with its live ref state: every branch name and the
resolved HEAD commit. Both are read from the object store on each call, so an
empty repo reports no branches and an empty head rather than failing. A repo
outside the caller's scope is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

patch.summary:
setVisibility flips a repo's public bit, the one mutable repo setting today.
Public grants ANONYMOUS fetch only; push and the whole control plane stay
org-authed.
patch.description:
setVisibility flips a repo's public bit, the one mutable repo setting today.
Public grants ANONYMOUS fetch only; push and the whole control plane stay
org-authed. Returns the updated repo.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to update, from the :name path segment.

get.summary: browseBlob returns one file's bytes at one revision.
get.description:
browseBlob returns one file's bytes at one revision. Text comes back verbatim,
binary comes back base64, and a file past the 1 MiB view cap comes back marked
truncated with NO content — the client is expected to clone instead.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path is repo-relative; empty is the tree root. Traversal is stripped.

get.summary:
browseCommits walks a ref's history newest first, or one path's history when a
path is given.
get.description:
browseCommits walks a ref's history newest first, or one path's history when a
path is given. There is no cursor: the page is the newest `limit` commits.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the branch, tag or commit to walk back from; empty means HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path narrows the history to commits touching it; empty walks the whole ref.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Anything not positive means 50; the cap is 100.

post.summary:
gc repacks a repo into one bitmapped pack and rewrites its commit-graph, so
the next clone reuses the bitmap instead of walking the whole object graph.
Idempotent, and safe to interrupt — git swaps both artifacts atomically.
post.description:
gc repacks a repo into one bitmapped pack and rewrites its commit-graph, so
the next clone reuses the bitmap instead of walking the whole object graph.
Idempotent, and safe to interrupt — git swaps both artifacts atomically. It
runs under one pack slot with the same memory bounds as a clone, so it can
block behind heavy pack traffic rather than compete with it. Storage usage is
re-measured afterwards, since a repack reclaims space.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

post.summary:
mirror imports an external git repository into the caller's repo, provisioning
it on first use.
post.description:
mirror imports an external git repository into the caller's repo, provisioning
it on first use. Fetch is FORCED and covers every ref, so a first call clones
the source and a repeat call re-syncs it — the endpoint is idempotent by mirror
semantics. Mirrored bytes are metered exactly like a push, and a push.landed
event is emitted for the default branch so the code index picks the repo up.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the local repo to mirror into, from the :name path segment. It is
CREATED on first use.

get.summary: listMirrors returns a repo's outbound mirror targets — the downstream remotes
get.description:
listMirrors returns a repo's outbound mirror targets — the downstream remotes
the mirror reactor pushes to whenever a push lands here.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

delete.summary:
deleteMirror removes one outbound mirror target; later pushes stop being
forwarded to it.
delete.description:
deleteMirror removes one outbound mirror target; later pushes stop being
forwarded to it. Answers 204 with no body. Nothing is done to the downstream
remote itself — only this repo's intent to push there is dropped.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the row to remove, from the :id path segment.

post.summary:
pushFiles lands a set of files as one commit without a git client — the
hanzo.app builder's push.
post.description:
pushFiles lands a set of files as one commit without a git client — the
hanzo.app builder's push. The repo is CREATED on first push, the files are
merged onto the branch tip (unlisted files survive), and the same
push-to-deploy hook a real receive-pack fires is fired, so downstream this is
indistinguishable from a `git push`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

get.summary:
browseReadme returns the README at the tree root as plain text — unrendered, so
the caller decides how to present it.
get.description:
browseReadme returns the README at the tree root as plain text — unrendered, so
the caller decides how to present it. A repo with no README is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

get.summary:
browseRefs lists a repo's branches, tags and default branch — what a branch
picker needs in one call.
get.description:
browseRefs lists a repo's branches, tags and default branch — what a branch
picker needs in one call. Unlike the other read ops it tolerates a repo with no
commits: the ref sets come back empty and the default branch is still named.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

get.summary: listSubscriptions returns a repo's Slack subscriptions — which channels the
get.description:
listSubscriptions returns a repo's Slack subscriptions — which channels the
lifecycle notifier posts this repo's push and deploy events to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

delete.summary:
unsubscribe removes one Slack subscription from a repo; the notifier stops
posting that repo's events to that channel.
delete.description:
unsubscribe removes one Slack subscription from a repo; the notifier stops
posting that repo's events to that channel. Answers 204 with no body. An id
that is not this repo's subscription is not found.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the row to remove, from the :id path segment.

get.summary:
browseTree lists the immediate children of one directory at one revision,
directories before files.
get.description:
browseTree lists the immediate children of one directory at one revision,
directories before files. It does not recurse — walk down a level at a time.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the repo to read, from the :name path segment.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is a branch, tag or commit; empty means the repo's HEAD.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path is repo-relative; empty is the tree root. Traversal is stripped.

get.summary:
usage returns per-repo and total storage bytes for the caller's org — the
queryable, per-tenant number commerce and o11y meter on.
get.description:
usage returns per-repo and total storage bytes for the caller's org — the
queryable, per-tenant number commerce and o11y meter on. It spans EVERY
project sub-scope, unlike the repo list, so a billing consumer sees the whole
tenant footprint in one call. Sizes are last-measured values (create, push,
mirror and gc each re-measure), not a live walk of the disk.

binary.description: Binary marks content git could not treat as text; it comes back base64.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, empty when Truncated.

encoding.description: Encoding is how Content is carried: "utf8" verbatim, or "base64".

path.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path.

size.description: Size is the file's byte length in the repo, whatever was returned below.

truncated.description:
Truncated marks a file past the 1 MiB view cap. No content is sent —
clone the repo for it.

authorEmail.description: AuthorEmail is the commit author's email.

authorName.description: AuthorName is the commit author's name.

date.description: Date is the author date, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: Message is the commit's SUBJECT — its first line only.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash.

shortSha.description: ShortSHA is the abbreviated hash a UI displays.

maintained.description: Maintained is always true; the call fails rather than reporting false.

repo.description: Repo is the repo that was repacked.

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes is the size measured AFTER the repack — usually smaller, since
repacking drops the packs it supersedes.

data.description: Data holds the repo's outbound mirror targets.

host.description: Host is the target's lowercased hostname, taken from URL and never the body.

id.description: ID is the target's identifier ("mir_…"), the handle to remove it by.

repo.description: Repo is the repo whose advanced refs are pushed downstream.

url.description: URL is the canonical https remote, with any embedded credentials stripped.

name.description:
Name is the local repo to mirror into, from the :name path segment. It is
CREATED on first use.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope to land the repo in; empty uses the caller's own,
exactly as a create would.

source.description:
Source is the http(s) git URL to fetch from. The host is SSRF-guarded and
the shared mirror credential is only sent to allowlisted hosts.

name.description: Name is the repo to update, from the :name path segment.

public.description:
Public flips anonymous read access. Omit it and the request is refused —
there is nothing else to update yet.

branch.description:
Branch to advance; empty means "main". A fresh branch that is the repo's
first also becomes HEAD.

files.description:
Files are added to or overwritten on the branch tip — files already there
and not listed SURVIVE. At least one, at most 5000, 32 MiB each.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, carried per Encoding.

path.description: Path is repo-relative. Absolute or traversing paths are refused.

message.description: Message is the commit message; empty gets a generated one.

name.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

branch.description: Branch is the branch that was advanced, resolved (never empty).

cloneUrl.description: CloneURL is the repo's HTTPS remote.

commit.description: Commit is the new commit's full hash.

sshUrl.description: SSHURL is the repo's scp-style SSH remote.

content.description: Content is the file's text, verbatim and unrendered.

encoding.description: Encoding is always "utf8" — a README is text by definition.

path.description: Path is the file the README was found at (README.md, README, …).

branches.description: Branches are the repo's heads; empty on a repo with no commits.

name.description: Name is the short ref name ("main", "v1.2.0"), not the full refs/… path.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash the ref resolves to.

default.description: Default is the branch name a caller gets when it asks for no ref.

tags.description: Tags are the repo's tags; empty when there are none.

name.description: Name is the short ref name ("main", "v1.2.0"), not the full refs/… path.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash the ref resolves to.

data.description: Data holds the repos in scope, most recently updated first.

branches.description:
Branches are the repo's branch names. Read live, so the detail view carries
them and a list row does not.

cloneUrl.description: CloneURL is the HTTPS smart-HTTP remote `git clone` takes.

defaultBranch.description: DefaultBranch is where HEAD points on a fresh repo ("main").

head.description: Head is the resolved HEAD commit, empty on an empty repo.

id.description: ID is the repo's stable, prefixed identifier ("repo_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the org-unique handle, and the last path segment of both URLs below.

org.description: Org owns the repo — the gateway-minted X-Org-Id, and the isolation key.

project.description:
Project is the optional sub-scope the repo lives in; absent for the org's
default scope.

public.description:
Public grants ANONYMOUS read (fetch) only; push and the whole control plane
stay org-authed.

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes is the repo's measured on-disk size, re-measured on create, after
each push, and after a gc. This is the number billing meters.

sshUrl.description: SSHURL is the scp-style SSH remote (git@host:org/repo.git).

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is RFC 3339 UTC, empty until the first write.

name.description:
Name is the repo's org-unique handle, from the :name path segment. A
trailing ".git" is stripped.

branches.description:
Branches are the repo's branch names. Read live, so the detail view carries
them and a list row does not.

cloneUrl.description: CloneURL is the HTTPS smart-HTTP remote `git clone` takes.

defaultBranch.description: DefaultBranch is where HEAD points on a fresh repo ("main").

head.description: Head is the resolved HEAD commit, empty on an empty repo.

id.description: ID is the repo's stable, prefixed identifier ("repo_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the org-unique handle, and the last path segment of both URLs below.

org.description: Org owns the repo — the gateway-minted X-Org-Id, and the isolation key.

project.description:
Project is the optional sub-scope the repo lives in; absent for the org's
default scope.

public.description:
Public grants ANONYMOUS read (fetch) only; push and the whole control plane
stay org-authed.

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes is the repo's measured on-disk size, re-measured on create, after
each push, and after a gc. This is the number billing meters.

sshUrl.description: SSHURL is the scp-style SSH remote (git@host:org/repo.git).

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is RFC 3339 UTC, empty until the first write.

channel.description: Channel is the Slack channel id or name the notifier posts to.

events.description: Events is the kind filter; absent means every deliverable kind.

id.description: ID is the subscription's identifier ("sub_…"), the handle to delete it by.

repo.description: Repo is the repo whose lifecycle events are delivered.

entries.description: Entries are the immediate children, directories before files.

mode.description: Mode is the octal git file mode ("100644", "040000", "120000").

name.description: Name is the entry's own name, no directory part.

path.description: Path is the entry's full repo-relative path.

size.description: Size is the file's byte length; 0 for a directory.

type.description: Type is "tree" for a directory, "blob" for a file.

repos.description: Repos is every repo the org owns, across every project sub-scope.

name.description: Name is the repo's org-unique handle.

project.description: Project is the sub-scope the repo lives in; absent for the default scope.

sizeBytes.description: SizeBytes is the repo's on-disk size at its last measurement.

totalBytes.description: TotalBytes is the sum over Repos — the org's whole git footprint.
